Name: Information use
Definition: The purpose or significance for which material is classified in a particular context. A single item may carry more than one use classification simultaneously (e.g. a key deliverable that is also contextual knowledge for the client relationship). Use is assigned by a person or process; it is not an intrinsic property of the material itself.

Name: Work record
Definition: The material relates to a specific matter or remit and is classified primarily for matter management purposes. Work record classifications support retrieval, status tracking and matter reporting.
Governance note: Work record classifications are typically applied at the point of creation or filing by the matter team.

Name: Work record > general
Definition: The material forms part of the working record of a matter or remit. It is retained for completeness and audit purposes but has no specific significance beyond that context.
Governance note: Default classification for matter documents not otherwise flagged.

Name: Work record > key
Definition: The material represents an important milestone, deliverable or attribute of a matter or remit. It warrants specific attention in matter management, reporting or handover.
Governance note: Typical triggers: executed agreements, final legal opinions, completed compliance steps, approved budgets, court orders, closing sets. Should be applied selectively: not every document in a matter is key.

Name: Knowledge
Definition: The material has value beyond its originating matter or remit and is classified for organisational knowledge purposes. Knowledge classifications support retrieval, reuse and guidance across matters.
Governance note: Knowledge classifications involve a judgement about future value. They should be applied by someone with the authority to make that judgement, and reviewed periodically.

Name: Knowledge > contextual
Definition: The material is useful context for future work with the same client, counterparty or on the same subject matter. It informs future work (e.g. to ensure consistency or avoid contradicting a prior position) but has not been validated as reusable guidance for the organisation generally.
Governance note: No formal validation required, but the person classifying should have sufficient knowledge of the matter to assess relevance. Distinguished from inf-use-4 (good practice) by the absence of endorsement and the narrower audience: typically useful to those dealing with this client or subject matter, not the organisation at large.

Name: Knowledge > good practice
Definition: The material has been reviewed and endorsed as a useful example of good practice, suitable for guidance in similar future matters. It is available to the organisation generally, not only to those with prior involvement.
Governance note: Requires: designated review and endorsement by a responsible individual or body (e.g. practice group lead, knowledge lawyer). The endorsement and endorser should be recorded. Distinguished from inf-use-3 (contextual) by the formal endorsement step and broader intended audience.

Name: Knowledge > canonical
Definition: The material provides the organisation's definitive approach to a topic or type of work. Departure from a canonical asset requires explicit justification. Supersedes other guidance on the same topic.
Governance note: Requires: formal approval by a designated authority (e.g. practice head, knowledge committee, general counsel). Canonical assets should be actively maintained: ownership assigned, review cycle set, superseded assets flagged or withdrawn. In organisations without a formal knowledge management function, this level should be used sparingly.
